blink.title: Blink to find what moves
blink.body: SPHEREx photographs the whole sky again and again. Flip between two dates: stars stay put, but nearby stars, asteroids and comets jump. SPHEREx pixels are big, so most jumps are under one pixel — the crosshair shows where to look.

colours.title: 102 colours you can’t see
colours.body: SPHEREx sees infrared light, from 0.75 to 5 micrometres, in six groups called D1 to D6. We paint them with false colours so your eyes can tell them apart. Some cold objects only appear in D5 and D6.

mark.title: Mark the moving dot
mark.body: On a time-lapse, tap the dot on each frame. Your marks are compared with the predicted path and with what others marked. Many careful eyes measure motion better than one.

saturation.title: Too bright is a result too
saturation.body: Very bright stars overflow the detector, like a photo of the Sun. When that happens SkySwap says so instead of showing fake numbers.

kinds.mover: A moving source: it sits in a different place on each visit.
kinds.residual: A leftover from image subtraction, usually around a bright star.
kinds.single: Seen on one visit only — often a cosmic ray or detector glitch.
kinds.trail: A streak across the image, often a satellite or a fast object.
kinds.stationary: Something that doesn’t move between visits.
kinds.orphan: A detection with no partner on other visits.
